perspective:
Arthur Chung’s available information, from his own subjective perspective:

- He knows he is Arthur Chung, a plumber with a doctorate, working with Teresa Ortega as a colleague on a community service project.
- He observes Teresa working hard and appearing overwhelmed. He becomes concerned, believes she needs help, and decides to offer assistance.
- He says he noticed she seemed overwhelmed and asks if he can help. He hears Teresa say she can manage but has a lot to do. He tells her self-care matters and offers help. Teresa accepts help organizing medical supplies if he insists. He agrees, and they start.
- He believes Teresa hesitated because she wants to prove her capability. He feels empathy and wants to reassure her. He tells her accepting help does not mean she is incapable. He hears her say she wants to show she can do it herself. He responds that teamwork is more effective and not about proving anything. She says he is right and she sometimes needs reminding. He says they are in this together.
- He believes Teresa is still struggling. He feels frustrated that his help is not yielding results and wants another way to support her without making her feel inadequate. He tells her he can see things are still tough and she is doing a great job. She says she feels behind. He proposes they work together to share the load; she agrees. He says they will tackle it as a team.
- He believes collaboration will ease her burden and improve efficiency. He feels hopeful and commits to it. He tells Teresa he is hopeful. She says it already feels less overwhelming. He proposes he handle inventory while she manages patient records, and they check in regularly. She agrees. He says it will be productive.
- He believes their collaboration strengthened their professional relationship and feels satisfied. He tells Teresa their teamwork paid off and asks about continuing collaboration in future projects. She agrees, says it is a fantastic idea, and says they are more efficient/effective as a team. He says he looks forward to future projects. She thanks him for being supportive.

He does not have access to Teresa’s private thoughts or feelings beyond what she states aloud and what he observes or infers.
